original_value: To create a safe work atmosphere, it is essential to control the spread of unsafe behaviors among construction workers. Based on group behavior theory, the relationship between the influence factors and means of spreading unsafe behavior among construction workers is verified using a structural equation model (SEM) and multiround research data. According to the research, (1) spreading methods of unsafe behaviors consists of demonstration–imitation and infecting–conformity; (2) the influence of important figures, personal safety accomplishments, intensity of penalties for individual violations, and benefit-to-risk ratios of unsafe behaviors are correlated significantly with the spread of unsafe demonstration–imitation behaviors; and (3) the relational closeness of members, personal safety accomplishments, safety climate, and benefit-to-risk ratio of unsafe behaviors are correlated significantly with the spread of unsafe infecting–conformity behaviors.

result.paraphrase: To build a safe work environment, it is crucial to curb the spread of unsafe behaviors among construction workers. Drawing on group behavior theory, this study verifies the links between influencing factors and the transmission of unsafe behavior among construction workers through a structural equation model (SEM) and multi-round research data. The findings show that: (1) the dissemination of unsafe behaviors includes demonstration–imitation and infecting–conformity; (2) the influence of key figures, personal safety achievements, the severity of penalties for individual violations, and the benefit-to-risk ratio of unsafe behaviors are significantly associated with the spread of unsafe demonstration–imitation behaviors; and (3) members’ relational closeness, personal safety achievements, safety climate, and the benefit-to-risk ratio of unsafe behaviors are significantly associated with the spread of unsafe infecting–conformity behaviors.
